design: Each career story chains CSTR story pages the open pack wrote: an opening background, a middle page, a page leading into one sword fight that names the foe, and a closing page on how the ship was won; every page is shown until the player turns it, and the story ends on a turned page. Chains were picked so each reads in order (e.g. convict 21 -> transported 22 -> cane fields 14 -> raid 15 -> fight -> letter of marque 17). Nations keep a colour across eras: England the indentured, convicts and sea dogs; France emigrants, Huguenots, buccaneers; Holland merchants, the company and ship owners; Spain men of rank, coast guards, fortune seekers; eras add history where an entry fits (a failing colony in 1560 France, the company in 1620 Holland, the guarda costa in 1680 Spain). All 12 openings and all 7 fight lead-ins are used; no two careers of an era share a story. The Dutch 1560 career, which does not exist, is empty. The six famous expeditions show the command page (40) then the voyage out (3), no fight. No page used has a %s filler.
